body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across either platform — a quiet, unremarkable day by that measure. Spot gold (XAU/USD) is trading in the $4,390–$4,410 range this week, well off the all-time high of roughly $5,602 that gold touched on January 28, 2026, and easing further on Monday as strong US jobs data raised the odds of a near-term Fed rate move. That pullback context matters for reading today's contract book: several Kalshi strikes sit thousands of dollars above the current spot (up to $5,090 and beyond) simply because they were listed while gold was still near its January peak, not because traders expect an imminent return there.

The contract prices line up sensibly with that backdrop. Kalshi's September 30, 2026 settle above $4,370.99 contract is priced near 0.57/0.58, essentially a coin-flip, which is exactly what you'd expect for a strike sitting almost on top of today's ~$4,400 spot price. Further-out strikes fall off in a smooth, orderly way (0.44 at $4,410, 0.18 at $4,610, down to pennies above $4,900), with no gaps or crossed markets that would signal a stale quote. On Polymarket, the September touch low contracts — which pay out if gold dips to a given level intramonth rather than settles there — likewise price the $3,800–$4,000 touches cheaply (2–13 cents), consistent with gold trading comfortably above those floors right now.

The absence of arbitrage isn't surprising: Kalshi's contracts settle on a specific end-of-window price while Polymarket's are often touch (intraday low/high) or daily up/down bets, so even when headline numbers look close, the underlying resolution rules differ enough that an apparent gap usually reflects that structural difference rather than free money. Today the books were simply well-behaved on both sides.
headline: No arbitrage found as Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts price consistently with $4,390-$4,410 spot
